segments.text: The Kingdom of Cloudmere. Tomorrow is the Grand Harvest Festival, and nothing is ready.
The last Steward of Errands quit — he tried to do everything himself instead of delegating to knights.
You're here! Splendid. You're my new Steward of Errands. Command knights to handle each task, and visit the Bedrock Bazaar to recruit allies.
I'm Pip, your apprentice! I'll help you learn the ropes.
The clock tower chimes. Sundown is sixty minutes away. Go.
WEATHER ALERT: Storm clouds gathering over the Bazaar. Merchants preparing to cover stalls.
Thunder rumbles across the town square. The Bazaar merchants start pulling tarps over their wares. Pip looks up at the sky, worried.
Steward! The storm! The merchants are closing up! We have two minutes before the Bazaar shuts!
Rain lashes the cobblestones. Two minutes pass. Then — sunlight breaks through. The merchants uncover their stalls, grumbling.
That was close! The merchants are back. But we've lost time!
The Champion knight strides through the festival grounds. Every errand complete. Every stall in place. The smell of Greta's feast drifts from the kitchens.
Grand Harvest Festival: READY. All errands fulfilled before sundown.
Lanterns flicker to life across the square. Music rises from the stages. The foreign traders raise a toast in three languages.
You did it! On your first day as Steward! The Queen is delighted. The nobles have stopped feuding. Even Sir Cedric cracked a smile — and I didn't think that was possible.
We did it, Steward! All five errands! I can't believe it!
You lean against the castle wall, watching the festival come alive below. Pip hands you a mug of cider.
The Kingdom of Cloudmere celebrates. And you — the Steward of Errands — made it happen.
Sundown. The Grand Harvest Festival is incomplete.
The sun dips below the hills. Festival-goers arrive to half-built stalls and missing performers. Greta serves bread and cheese instead of a feast.
But the lanterns still glow. The people still gather. A festival half-done is still a festival.
We learned a lot today, Steward. Tomorrow we'll be faster. I kept notes!
Tomorrow, you'll know which knights to send, which allies to recruit, and which errands to tackle first.
